FACTS OF THE CASE 1.

Briefly stated, the facts of the petition are that on 29.09.2020, at about 05:30 p.m., one Sanjay Bhushan (since deceased) was going to Bhaina from Garh, on a motorcycle bearing registration no.
UP23AA-9522.

It has been alleged that when he reached near Badarkha Bridge, within the jurisdiction of PS Garhmukteshwar GT Road, Hapur, a canter bearing registration no. HR63D-2985 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle), came at a very high speed and hit the afore-said motorcycle of the victim with a great force.

It has been further alleged that the offending vehicle was being driven by its driver i.e. respondent no. 1 (R1) herein, at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner without taking necessary precautions at the time of the accident.
Allegedly, the deceased as aforesaid sustained grievous injuries after being hit by the offending vehicle and he was taken to Uma Lok hospital, Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN

The postmortem of the body of deceased was conducted at District Mortuary, Meerut.

420/2020, for the offences u/s 279/338/304-A IPC.
The present claim petition thereon came to be filed in due course for the petitioners being the LRs of the deceased/victim and against the respondents on 07.11.2020.

Issue wise findings Issue no.1 11.

Whether respondent no. 1 was driving the offending vehicle i.e. Canter no. HR63D-2985 on 29.09.2020 at about 05:30 p.m. near Badarkha Bridge, within the jurisdiction of PS Garhmukteshwar GT Road, Hapur, in a rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Sh. Sanjay Bhushan S/o Mahipal? OPP 12.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a HARUN PRATAP Date:
PRATAP 2025.10.06 16:48:54 +0530 criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs Amir Chand & Ors, 2011 (1) SCR 1906 (Civil Appeal No. 1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
13.

In the present case, the petitioners have examined the eye witness of the accident namely Sh.
Tarun Kumar Rawat as their star witness to prove the contentions regarding the claim for compensation, apart from examining wife of the deceased victim as PW2 and PW1 respectively.
Both the afore- said witnesses have categorically stated in their examination on oath that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent act of respondent no. 1 in driving the offending vehicle.

The said contentions are duly corroborated by the findings of the police as mentioned in the site plan,
mechanical inspection report, Charge sheet, postmortem report along with other documents pertaining to criminal case in respect of the incident in question brought on record as Ex. PW1/1 (colly) and no ground has been made out by the respondents to disbelieve the same.

The testimony Pushpa vs Mahesh Kumar Sharma on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152046945/
4 of both the witnesses for the petitioner has remained consistent and no doubt has been raised by the respondents to disbelieve the same.

The sole contention raised by the respondents regarding delay in registration of FIR has also been duly explained in the FIR itself as it has been specifically stated therein that the FIR was registered after a delay of 4 days from the accident as the HARUN PRATAP Date:
PRATAP 2025.10.06 16:49:06 +0530 complainant was in shock and grief due to the death of his son i.e. victim in the present case.

At the same time, the eye witness examined as PW2 has also explained his presence at the spot of the accident in great details and no material has been brought on record by the respondents to disbelieve the same.

The PW2 has also explained the non inclusion of his name as an eye witness in the criminal case charge-sheet by the police during his cross- examination and in absence of any evidence being led by the respondents to the contrary, the Tribunal has no ground to disbelieve the testimony of PW2.

Respondent no.1 i.e.
driver, respondent no. 02 i.e. owner of the offending vehicle and respondent no. 3 i.e.
Insurance Company, have neither impeached the testimony of PW-1 & PW-2 nor they have led any defence evidence to substantiate their claim that the accident was caused due to fault of the deceased or that they have been falsely implicated in the present case.

14. The very fact that R-1 has already been specifically arrayed as an accused in case FIR No.
420/2020, PS Garhmukteshwar, GT Road, Hapur, for the offences u/s 279/338/304-A IPC is also a strong circumstance to support the above said testimony of PW-1 and PW-2 on these issues.
The copies of FIR, Site plan, report u/s 173 Cr.PC, mechanical inspection report and postmortem report brought on record also corroborate the oral testimony of PW-1 & PW2.

Moreover, the position of law in this regard Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:

Arising out of SLP (C ) No. 10351/2019, wherein it has been held that:-
"It is settled in law that once a charge-sheet has been filed and the driver has been held negligent, no further evidence is required to prove that the bus was being negligently driven by the bus driver.
Even if the eye witnesses are not examined, that will not be fatal to prove the death of the deceased due to negligence of the bus driver."

Besides the above, respondent no. 1 namely Mahesh Kumar Sharma was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the depositions being made by PW-1 regarding the above accident and its manner etc., but he has not done so.

Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi).

17. Having ruled so, this Tribunal now proceeds to assess the wrongful act, neglect or default of R-1,
if any, in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Admittedly, R-1 has not explained the circumstances under which his vehicle (i.e. the offending vehicle) hit the deceased Sh. Sanjay Bhushan.

In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the deceased or any other such person, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

In view of the above discussion, this tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time leading to the fatal injuries to the deceased Sh. Sanjay Bhushan.

Issue no. (ii) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

20

. On the basis of findings upon issue no. (i), it is clear that the incident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by R-1 and fatal injuries had been caused to the deceased in the incident.

Hence, the petitioners being the wife, children and parents are entitled to compensation in this case as the claim of the petitioners being dependents of the deceased has neither been denied nor disputed in any manner by the respondents during the entire proceedings.
21. The issue at hand is accordingly decided in favour of the petitioners and against the respondents.
LIABILITY 22.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
The respondent no. 1 Mahesh Kumar Sharma is the principal tort feasor being driver, while the respondent no. 2 is vicariously liable being the owner of the offending vehicle.

Herein, it is HARUN PRATAP PRATAP 2025.10.06 16:49:26 +0530 pertinent to note that the respondent no. 3 i.e. Insurance Company has specifically admitted in its written statement that the offending vehicle was duly insured at the time of accident with respondent no. 1 vide insurance policy no.
35380231200300000519, in the name of M/S Bhumika Roadlines i.e. respondent no. 2 (R2), with its validity from 06.06.2020 to 05.06.2021.
At the same time, the respondent no. 3 has failed to bring on record or to prove any breach of the terms or conditions of the said insurance policy by the respondents no. 1 and 2 in any manner.

23. Hence, on the basis of entire above stated facts and circumstances and discussion of evidence,
this Tribunal is of the opinion that respondent no. 3 i.e. insurance company, is liable to pay the entire compensation to the petitioner on behalf of respondent no. 1 and 2, without any recovery rights.
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 24.

As far as computation of compensation is concerned, the same shall be under the following heads :-
MEDICAL EXPENSES 25.

It is clear from above stated facts and circumstances that the deceased had expired soon after the accident and no medical expenditure was undertaken by the petitioner in the treatment of the deceased before his death.

Hence, petitioner is not entitled to any compensation under this head on Pushpa vs Mahesh Kumar Sharma on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152046945/
7 account of absence of any evidence brought on record in this regard.
LOSS OF DEPENDENCY 26.

In the present case, perusal of the Aadhar card of deceased Sh. Sanjay Bhushan Ex. PW1/3 reveals that date of birth of the deceased was HARUN PRATAP PRATAP 2025.10.06 16:49:30 +0530 01.01.1979 and the same has not been disputed in any manner by the respondents.

Therefore, the deceased was thus aged about 41 years 8 months at the time of the incident resulting in his death on 29.09.2020.
27.

Petitioner no.1 Smt. Pushpa (PW1) in her deposition has stated that at the time of accident, her deceased husband was doing a job in BMR Ultrasound, Garh Chopla and that he was earning Rs.
16,000/- per month.
The petitioners have also brought on record a salary certificate purportedly issued by the employer of the deceased victim as Ex. PW1/4.

The original of the said document brought by the petitioner has neither been disputed nor denied by the respondents in any manner and not even a single suggestion to the contrary has been given by the respondents to the PW1 during the latter's cross-examination.

Hence, the income of deceased is hereby assessed to be Rs.
16,000/- per month.

28. Furthermore, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court titled as "National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. (2017) 16 SCC 680", 25% addition shall be given to the deceased towards future prospects as he was between 41 to 50 years of age at the time of incident and was self employed.

29. As borne out from the record, the deceased Sh. Sanjay Bhushan was having his wife, two children and his aged mother and father as dependents upon him on the date of the incident.
Therefore, all the five original petitioners shall be treated as dependents of the deceased for the purpose of the present petition.

Furthermore, since there were total 05 dependents of HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:

Therefore, in the entire given facts and circumstances, deduction of 1/4th of total income is made for personal living expenses of deceased.
Hence, an amount of Rs. 5,000/- (Rs. 20,000/4) is required to be deducted from annual income of deceased.

Finally, annual dependency of dependents is calculated as under (annual income) - (annual expenses of deceased) i.e. (Rs. 2,40,000/- - Rs. 60,000/-) = Rs.
1,80,000/- per annum.

LOSS OF CONSORTIUM / LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION 31.

In "Magma Vs. General Insurance Co. Ltd Vs. Nanu Ram & Ors". 2018 ACJ 2782, it was observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court that 'consortium' is a compendious term, which encompasses 'spousal consortium', 'parental consortium' and 'filial consortium'.

sentences.text: The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his entire family.

HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2025.10.06 16:49:43 +0530 Spousal Consortium allows compensation to surviving spouse for loss of 'company, society, co-operation, affection and aid of the other in every conjugal relation'.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court further observed in said judgment that parental consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of 'parental aid, protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training.
Similarly, filial consortium is to be granted to each of the surviving dependent parents on the death of their child.

32. In the facts and circumstances of the present case, the computation of compensation under this head is as follows :
Filial Consortium : Rs. 96,000/- (Rs. 48,000/- X 2)

Spousal Consortium : Rs.
48,000/- (Rs. 48,000/- X 1) Parental Consortium : Rs. 96,000/- (Rs. 48,000/- X 2)

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities.
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a HARUN PRATAP Date:
PRATAP 2025.10.06 16:48:54 +0530 criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs Amir Chand & Ors, 2011 (1) SCR 1906 (Civil Appeal No. 1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
13.
In the present case, the petitioners have examined the eye witness of the accident namely Sh.
Tarun Kumar Rawat as their star witness to prove the contentions regarding the claim for compensation, apart from examining wife of the deceased victim as PW2 and PW1 respectively.
Both the afore- said witnesses have categorically stated in their examination on oath that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent act of respondent no. 1 in driving the offending vehicle.
The PW2 has also explained the non inclusion of his name as an eye witness in the criminal case charge-sheet by the police during his cross- examination and in absence of any evidence being led by the respondents to the contrary, the Tribunal has no ground to disbelieve the testimony of PW2.
Respondent no.1 i.e.
driver, respondent no. 02 i.e. owner of the offending vehicle and respondent no. 3 i.e.
Insurance Company, have neither impeached the testimony of PW-1 & PW-2 nor they have led any defence evidence to substantiate their claim that the accident was caused due to fault of the deceased or that they have been falsely implicated in the present case.
The evidence of the star witness in this case i.e. PW-2, on the aspect of rash and negligent act of respondent no. 1 while driving the offending vehicle, has remained unimpeached and his testimony has to be accepted on its face value itself as the same has successfully stood the test of cross-examination and no material has been brought on record by the respondents to negate the same.
Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi).
16.
In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that the offending vehicle was being driven by R-1 indeed at the time of incident and the fatal injuries to the deceased took place on account of the incident in question itself.
Admittedly, R-1 has not explained the circumstances under which his vehicle (i.e. the offending vehicle) hit the deceased Sh. Sanjay Bhushan.
In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the deceased or any other such person, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion, this tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time leading to the fatal injuries to the deceased Sh. Sanjay Bhushan.
Furthermore, in view of the medical records, postmortem report placed on record by the petitioner, no doubt or dispute is left regarding the fatal injuries to the deceased Sh. Sanjay Bhushan in the above accident.
. On the basis of findings upon issue no. (i), it is clear that the incident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by R-1 and fatal injuries had been caused to the deceased in the incident.
Hence, the petitioners being the wife, children and parents are entitled to compensation in this case as the claim of the petitioners being dependents of the deceased has neither been denied nor disputed in any manner by the respondents during the entire proceedings.
The respondent no. 1 Mahesh Kumar Sharma is the principal tort feasor being driver, while the respondent no. 2 is vicariously liable being the owner of the offending vehicle.
At the same time, the respondent no. 3 has failed to bring on record or to prove any breach of the terms or conditions of the said insurance policy by the respondents no. 1 and 2 in any manner.
23. Hence, on the basis of entire above stated facts and circumstances and discussion of evidence,
this Tribunal is of the opinion that respondent no. 3 i.e. insurance company, is liable to pay the entire compensation to the petitioner on behalf of respondent no. 1 and 2, without any recovery rights.
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 24.
It is clear from above stated facts and circumstances that the deceased had expired soon after the accident and no medical expenditure was undertaken by the petitioner in the treatment of the deceased before his death.
Therefore, the deceased was thus aged about 41 years 8 months at the time of the incident resulting in his death on 29.09.2020.
27.
30. Moreover, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of "Sarla Verma &
Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr"., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitutional Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of " National Insurance Company Ltd.
Vs Pranay Sethi & Ors".
